authorization.context: Reply to the decision packet message of 2026-11-15 offering: 1 keep held, 2 approve as PUBLIC-BY-DESIGN as is (providerName included, no route change), 3 approve after removing providerName. The owner first replied approve option 3; after being told that option would hold the OIDC start and callback credits and that the app never reads providerName, the owner replied 2.

publicFields: available: whether the email's domain is a verified domain of an enabled OIDC provider in the same employer
providerId: numeric, sequential provider ID, needed to build the start URL
providerName: free text chosen by the employer admin; it can contain the employer's name
startUrl: /api/auth/sso/start?providerId=...&loginHint=... where the hint is the caller's own email echoed back
excludedFields: worker, membership, session, bank, payroll or audit data
client IDs or secrets and IdP entity or certificate data
approvedDisclosure: Anonymous callers can learn that an email domain uses single sign-on and receive the provider ID and the employer-chosen provider name; every other case returns one identical available:false body. The runtime flag keeps the endpoint off by default in production.
